subsystems.responsibility: Centralized dedup-aware notification dispatch to Telegram, Discord, Email, Slack, and Webhook channels
subsystems.description: Event-driven notification routing subsystem. Write_immutable_log is called unconditionally first, then _should_alert() checks Redis SETNX dedup (fail-open: always alert on Redis failure). If dedup passes, fires notifications: Telegram (25+ event type templates, 4096-char HTML via background thread), Discord (via requests.post, thread or inline), Email via Resend (thread, HTML), Slack (demo requests only), and custom HMAC-signed webhook (LLM firewall only). Telegram templates include alert_canary_triggered, alert_sandbox_entered, alert_sandbox_exfil, alert_dna_deviation, alert_ip_blocked, alert_timing_canary, alert_provenance_violation, alert_breach_found, alert_mirror_deep, alert_daily_summary, and 15+ module-specific templates. Events trigger notifications from 13+ subsystems (Cowrie, BGP, Campaign Correlator, Credential Propagation, Supply Chain, LLM Honeypot, LLM Firewall, AIRS, Canary Service, Sandbox, Timing Canary, Honeytoken, Breach Monitor).

redis_usage.purpose: Dedup via Redis SETNX (120-300s TTL, fail-open: always alert)

background_workers: send_notification threads for Discord, Email, Webhook
logging_sources: Debug log lines on send failure
failure_modes: Fire-and-forget threads: failed notifications silently dropped
No dead-letter queue (Gap 3)
Telegram 400/rate limit: message silently lost
Discord webhook non-200: silently lost
Email via Resend API failure: silently lost
subsystems.recovery_behavior: No retry mechanism — fire-and-forget only
scalability_concerns: Thread-per-notification under attack volume
No thread pool cap can lead to thousands of notification threads

subsystems.responsibility: Orchestrate the 8 before_request middleware handlers, 1 route handler, and 3 after_request handlers that wrap every HTTP request
subsystems.description: Every HTTP request traverses 8 before_request middleware handlers: (1) check_xhr_for_state_change (line 960) — returns 403 if state-changing API request has no X-Requested-With and no origin gate bypass; (2) limit_request_size (line 986) — returns 413 if >16MB; (3) corpus_middleware (line 1208) — always writes to fingerprint Redis keys; (4) enforce_https (line 1212) — 301 redirect if HTTP+production; (5) add_request_id (line 1225) — sets request.id = UUID4[:8]; (6) update_session_activity (line 7068) — updates ActiveSession DB, 24h idle redirect, spawns _finalize_session_dna thread on expiry; (7) honey_token_check (line 7288) — 8+ branch decision tree (static, whitelisted, authenticated, sandboxed, provenance, API key honey, legitimate, sensitive, reverse canary, suspicious technique, SQL pattern); (8) check_ip_blocklist (line 8411) — 403 if IP in blocklist. After_request: (9) set_security_headers (line 1177) — CSP/HSTS/XFO, (10) log_response (line 1233) — debug log, (11) track_dna_event (line 7112) — SessionEvent DB write, spawns DNA thread every 5th event. The require_auth decorator (line 7394) gates protected routes.

redis_usage.purpose: Fingerprint corpus writes from corpus_middleware

daemon_threads: _finalize_session_dna — spawned on session expiry via update_session_activity
background_workers: _record_and_score_dna — spawned every 5th auth request via track_dna_event
failure_modes: Any middleware can short-circuit the entire request lifecycle
Thread-per-request under attack for DNA and predictive threads
subsystems.recovery_behavior: Middleware chain is per-request; no cross-request state recovery needed
subsystems.latency_expectation: Total middleware stack: 5-50ms per request (depends on DB writes in session update)
scalability_concerns: 8 middleware handlers per request adds latency
Suspicious_technique_detected spawns thread per suspicious request
Session activity DB write per authenticated request

subsystems.responsibility: Redis-based leader election that ensures exactly one gunicorn worker runs background engines (Cowrie, Campaign, ASN, BGP, scheduler)
subsystems.description: The _engine_supervisor daemon thread (started at import time in main.py:12254) acquires the Redis lock wraithwall:engine_leader via SET NX with 45s TTL and 15s heartbeat. Only the leader starts: APScheduler (9 jobs), cowrie watcher (daemon threads for file tail, event workers, alert worker), campaign engine (get_correlator singleton), propagation network (auto_rotate daemon), ASN engine (get_service singleton), BGP monitor (RIPE WS daemon). Unconditionally started (not leader-gated): detonate worker loop (BRPOP daemon), keep_alive ping daemon. Without Redis lock, every gunicorn worker runs all engines — N duplicates.

redis_usage.purpose: Leader lock for engine supervisor (SET NX, 45s TTL, 15s heartbeat)

failure_modes: Redis failure: every worker runs all engines (N duplicates)
Lock expiry before heartbeat: unnecessary failover
No lock release on process crash: standby waits for TTL expiry (45s)
subsystems.recovery_behavior: atexit handler releases lock on graceful shutdown; standby acquires on TTL expiry
scalability_concerns: If Redis fails, N gunicorn workers run N × engines (N duplicates)
9 APScheduler jobs with max_instances=1: model_retrained can skip
